Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of call
- Use case: Opsly wants to reduce per-request latency for large-vector searches and move embeddings inference off-prem for scale.
- Key success criteria called out: P99 latency <120ms, regional failover for US/EU, and per-embedding cost target ~$0.0008.

Open items we agreed to confirm
1) Stakeholder map: economic buyer, procurement contact, and security lead for the review.
2) Systems in scope for the security questionnaire (where customer data touches Redwood).
3) Procurement timeline / contract owner and any purchasing constraints.

Action items
- Emily: please confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact, and attach Opsly systems inventory if available (S3 buckets, DBs, Redis instances, etc.).
- Redwood (me): schedule a 30–45m security kickoff once we have stakeholders; send our intake form and SOC2 artifacts in advance.
- Rishi: I’ll loop you in for success-criteria alignment + POC sizing once the stakeholder map is confirmed.

Attachments: security-intake-form.docx (filled by Opsly), SOC2-Redwood-2025.pdf (Redwood)

Proposed security kickoff window: Tue Feb 24 or Wed Feb 25, mornings PST. Let me know which works for you.

Thanks — Lauren

Lauren / Rishi — I pulled together intake answers and an initial scope summary to use as the pre-read. I can convert these into the .docx if you want, or paste into email to Opsly. Key points below: 

1) Systems in scope (based on Opsly spreadsheet)- Customer upload S3 buckets: inbound customer files (encrypted at rest)- Embeddings cache: Redis cluster (AWS ElastiCache) — contains derived embeddings, not raw PII- Embeddings inference: ephemeral GPU hosts in Redwood Dedicated for model inference- Metadata DB: Postgres (customer user IDs, non-sensitive metadata)

2) Data residency & KMS- Default: customer data encrypted at rest with AWS KMS. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) for private deployments and can integrate with HSM for Private installs.- We will provide key-rotation notes and limited KMS access audit logs for Opsly

3) Logging & evidence- Audit logs: request-level traces for inference calls (timestamp, model, route, token usage) retained 90 days by default; extended retention available as an add-on.- Auth: token issuance and rotation logs available; we can provide IAM mapping and service account audit trails.

4) Minimal environment required for POC- S3 bucket for sample data (Opsly gives read-only access)- Test Redis instance or RW access to a staging cluster- Demo dataset of ~100k vectors to validate perf targets

5) Questions for Opsly (to include in kickoff)- Are there any regulatory constraints (e.g., PCI, HIPAA) that change our standard controls?- Are there specific IP allowlists or dedicated network paths required for integrations?

I can convert this into the security-intake-form.docx and attach. Also attaching the SOC2-Redwood-2025.pdf is helpful as pre-read.

Monica Patel
